sanskrit: atha rātryāṃ vyatītāyāṃ viśvāmitro mahāmuniḥ āpṛcchya tau ca rājānau jagāmottaraparvatam
english: Then, when the night had passed, the great sage Viśvāmitra took leave of both kings and departed toward the northern mountain.

sanskrit: viśvāmitro gate rājā vaidehaṃ mithilādhipam āpṛcchyātha jagāmāśu rājā daśarathaḥ purīm
english: After Viśvāmitra had departed, king Daśaratha quickly took leave of the Videha king, the lord of Mithilā, and returned to his own city.

sanskrit: atha rājā videhānāṃ dadau kanyādhanaṃ bahu gavāṃ śatasahasrāṇi bahūni mithileśvaraḥ
english: Then the king of the Videhas, the lord of Mithilā, bestowed lavish bridal gifts — many hundreds of thousands of cows.

sanskrit: kambalānāṃ ca mukhyānāṃ kṣaumakoṭyambarāṇi ca hastyaśvarathapādātaṃ divyarūpaṃ svalaṃkṛtam
english: Foremost blankets and tens of millions of silk garments; elephants, horses, chariots, and foot-soldiers of divine appearance, richly adorned.

sanskrit: dadau kanyā pitā tāsāṃ dāsīdāsam anuttamam hiraṇyasya suvarṇasya muktānāṃ vidrumasya ca
english: The father of the brides gave unsurpassed female and male attendants, as well as silver, gold, pearls, and coral.

sanskrit: dadau paramasaṃhṛṣṭaḥ kanyādhanam anuttamam dattvā bahudhanaṃ rājā samanujñāpya pārthivam
english: With supreme delight the king gave these peerless bridal gifts; having bestowed abundant wealth, he duly took leave of the king.

sanskrit: praviveśa svanilayaṃ mithilāṃ mithileśvaraḥ rājāpy ayodhyādhipatiḥ saha putrair mahātmabhiḥ
english: The lord of Mithilā re-entered his own abode, Mithilā; and the king, the lord of Ayodhyā, departed together with his noble sons.

sanskrit: ṛṣīn sarvān puraskṛtya jagāma sabalānugaḥ gacchantaṃ tu naravyāghraṃ sarṣisaṃghaṃ sarāghavam
english: Placing all the sages at the fore, he set out with his army and retinue; and as that tiger among men, Rāghava, marched with the host of sages—

sanskrit: ghorāḥ sma pakṣiṇo vāco vyāharanti tatas tataḥ bhaumāś caiva mṛgāḥ sarve gacchanti sma pradakṣiṇam
english: — dreadful birds uttered cries here and there, and all the earthly beasts moved in a clockwise direction around him.

sanskrit: tān dṛṣṭvā rājaśārdūlo vasiṣṭhaṃ paryapṛcchata asaumyāḥ pakṣiṇo ghorā mṛgāś cāpi pradakṣiṇāḥ kim idaṃ hṛdayotkampi mano mama viṣīdati
english: Seeing these omens, the tiger among kings questioned Vasiṣṭha: "The birds are ominous and terrible, the beasts too go clockwise — what is this? My heart trembles and my mind is troubled."

sanskrit: rājño daśarathasyaitac chrutvā vākyaṃ mahān ṛṣiḥ uvāca madhurāṃ vāṇīṃ śrūyatām asya yat phalam
english: Having heard these words of king Daśaratha, the great sage spoke in a sweet voice: "Hear what fruit these omens portend."

sanskrit: upasthitaṃ bhayaṃ ghoraṃ divyaṃ pakṣimukhāc cyutam mṛgāḥ praśamayanty ete saṃtāpas tyajyatām ayam
english: "A terrible, celestial danger has been declared by the birds; these beasts are propitious and allay it — let this anxiety be abandoned."

sanskrit: teṣāṃ saṃvadatāṃ tatra vāyuḥ prādur babhūva ha kampayan medinīṃ sarvāṃ pātayaṃś ca drumāñ śubhān
english: While they were conversing there, a fierce wind arose, shaking the entire earth and toppling the stately trees.

sanskrit: tamasā saṃvṛtaḥ sūryaḥ sarvā na prababhur diśaḥ bhasmanā cāvṛtaṃ sarvaṃ saṃmūḍham iva tad balam
english: The sun was shrouded in darkness, the directions could not be discerned, everything was covered with ash, and the whole army seemed bewildered.

sanskrit: vasiṣṭha ṛṣayaś cānye rājā ca sasutas tadā sasaṃjñā iva tatrāsan sarvam anyad vicetanam
english: Vasiṣṭha, the other sages, and the king with his sons retained their senses, while all else present seemed to lose consciousness.

sanskrit: tasmiṃs tamasi ghore tu bhasmacchanneva sā camūḥ dadarśa bhīmasaṃkāśaṃ jaṭāmaṇḍaladhāriṇam
english: In that terrible darkness, with the army as though smothered in ash, they beheld a figure of fearsome aspect wearing a crown of matted locks—

sanskrit: kailāsam iva durdharṣaṃ kālāgnim iva duḥsaham jvalantam iva tejobhir durnirīkṣyaṃ pṛthagjanaiḥ
english: — as unconquerable as mount Kailāsa, as unbearable as the fire at the end of time, blazing with such splendour that common folk could scarce behold him.

sanskrit: skandhe cāsajya paraśuṃ dhanur vidyudgaṇopamam pragṛhya śaramukhyaṃ ca tripuraghnaṃ yathā haram
english: With an axe slung upon his shoulder, a bow resembling a mass of lightning in his hands, and bearing the foremost arrow — like Hara who destroyed the three cities.

sanskrit: taṃ dṛṣṭvā bhīmasaṃkāśaṃ jvalantam iva pāvakam vasiṣṭhapramukhā viprā japahomaparāyaṇāḥ saṃgatā munayaḥ sarve saṃjajalpur atho mithaḥ
english: Beholding him of terrifying aspect, blazing as if he were fire, the brāhmaṇas headed by Vasiṣṭha — all the sages devoted to prayer and oblation — gathered and began to murmur to one another.

sanskrit: kaccit pitṛvadhāmarṣī kṣatraṃ notsādayiṣyati pūrvaṃ kṣatravadhaṃ kṛtvā gatamanyur gatajvaraḥ kṣatrasyotsādanaṃ bhūyo na khalv asya cikīrṣitam
english: "Can it be that this one, still wrathful over his father's slaying, intends to annihilate the kṣatriyas? Having once massacred the kṣatriyas, his rage and fever were spent — surely he does not now intend their destruction again?"

sanskrit: evam uktvārghyam ādāya bhārgavaṃ bhīmadarśanam ṛṣayo rāma rāmeti madhurāṃ vācam abruvan
english: Having spoken thus, the sages took the ceremonial offering and, approaching that fearsome son of Bhṛgu's line, addressed him in gentle words: "Rāma, Rāma!"

sanskrit: pratigṛhya tu tāṃ pūjām ṛṣidattāṃ pratāpavān rāmaṃ dāśarathiṃ rāmo jāmadagnyo 'bhyabhāṣata
english: Accepting that homage offered by the sages, the mighty Rāma, son of Jamadagni, then addressed Rāma, son of Daśaratha.

sanskrit: rāma dāśarathe vīra vīryaṃ te śrūyate 'dhutam dhanuṣo bhedanaṃ caiva nikhilena mayā śrutam
english: "O heroic Rāma, son of Daśaratha, your wondrous valour has come to my ears; the breaking of the bow also I have heard in full detail."

sanskrit: tad adbhutam acintyaṃ ca bhedanaṃ dhanuṣas tvayā tac chrutvāham anuprāpto dhanur gṛhyāparaṃ śubham
english: "That breaking of the bow by you is wondrous and inconceivable; having heard of it, I have come, bringing yet another auspicious bow."

sanskrit: tad idaṃ ghorasaṃkāśaṃ jāmadagnyaṃ mahad dhanuḥ pūrayasva śareṇaiva svabalaṃ darśayasva ca
english: "This great bow of Jamadagni's race, of terrifying aspect — string it with an arrow, and reveal your own strength."

sanskrit: tad ahaṃ te balaṃ dṛṣṭvā dhanuṣo 'sya prapūraṇe dvandvayuddhaṃ pradāsyāmi vīryaślāghyam idaṃ tava
english: "When I have seen your strength in stringing this bow, I shall offer you single combat — this is the true test of your valour."

sanskrit: tasya tad vacanaṃ śrutvā rājā daśarathas tadā viṣaṇṇavadano dīnaḥ prāñjalir vākyam abravīt
english: Hearing those words of his, king Daśaratha, his face downcast and wretched, spoke with folded hands.

sanskrit: kṣatraroṣāt praśāntas tvaṃ brāhmaṇasya mahāyaśāḥ bālānāṃ mama putrāṇām abhayaṃ dātum arhasi
english: "You, of great renown among brāhmaṇas, have calmed the wrath born of the kṣatriya quarrel — you ought to grant safety to my young sons."

sanskrit: bhārgavāṇāṃ kule jātaḥ svādhyāyavrataśālinām sahasrākṣe pratijñāya śastraṃ nikṣiptavān asi
english: "Born in the lineage of the Bhārgavas, distinguished for their vows of sacred study, you made a promise to the thousand-eyed Indra and laid down your weapons."

sanskrit: sa tvaṃ dharmaparo bhūtvā kāśyapāya vasuṃdharām dattvā vanam upāgamya mahendrakṛtaketanaḥ
english: "You, being devoted to dharma, gave the earth to Kaśyapa and retired to the forest — you whose dwelling was established by Mahendra."

sanskrit: mama sarvavināśāya saṃprāptas tvaṃ mahāmune na caikasmin hate rāme sarve jīvāmahe vayam
english: "You have come, O great sage, for my total ruin; for if but one Rāma is slain, we cannot all of us survive."

sanskrit: bruvaty evaṃ daśarathe jāmadagnyaḥ pratāpavān anādṛtyaiva tad vākyaṃ rāmam evābhyabhāṣata
english: While Daśaratha was speaking thus, the mighty son of Jamadagni disregarded those words entirely and spoke only to Rāma.

sanskrit: ime dve dhanuṣī śreṣṭhe divye lokābhiviśrute dṛḍhe balavatī mukhye sukṛte viśvakarmaṇā
english: "These two are the foremost of bows — divine, renowned throughout the worlds, firm, powerful, supreme, and well crafted by Viśvakarman."

sanskrit: atisṛṣṭaṃ surair ekaṃ tryambakāya yuyutsave tripuraghnaṃ naraśreṣṭha bhagnaṃ kākutstha yat tvayā
english: "One was bestowed by the gods upon the three-eyed Tryambaka, eager for battle — that Tripura-slaying bow which you, best of men, O Kākutstha, have broken."

sanskrit: idaṃ dvitīyaṃ durdharṣaṃ viṣṇor dattaṃ surottamaiḥ samānasāraṃ kākutstha raudreṇa dhanuṣā tv idam
english: "This second bow, O Kākutstha, unconquerable, was given to Viṣṇu by the greatest of gods — it is of equal substance to the bow of Rudra."

sanskrit: tadā tu devatāḥ sarvāḥ pṛcchanti sma pitāmaham śitikaṇṭhasya viṣṇoś ca balābalanirīkṣayā
english: "At that time all the gods questioned the Grandfather Brahmā, wishing to assess the comparative strength of Śitikaṇṭha and Viṣṇu."

sanskrit: abhiprāyaṃ tu vijñāya devatānāṃ pitāmahaḥ virodhaṃ janayām āsa tayoḥ satyavatāṃ varaḥ
english: "Understanding the intention of the gods, the Grandfather, best among those who hold to truth, caused a conflict to arise between the two."

sanskrit: virodhe ca mahad yuddham abhavad romaharṣaṇam śitikaṇṭhasya viṣṇoś ca parasparajayaiṣiṇoḥ
english: "In that conflict a great battle occurred, causing the hair to stand on end, as Śitikaṇṭha and Viṣṇu each strove to vanquish the other."

sanskrit: tadā taj jṛmbhitaṃ śaivaṃ dhanur bhīmaparākramam huṃkāreṇa mahādevaḥ stambhito 'tha trilocanaḥ
english: "Then the bow of Śiva, of terrible might, was made to yawn open; and by Viṣṇu's humkāra Mahādeva, the three-eyed one, was paralysed."

sanskrit: devais tadā samāgamya sarṣisaṃghaiḥ sacāraṇaiḥ yācitau praśamaṃ tatra jagmatus tau surottamau
english: "Then the gods, assembling together with the hosts of sages and the Cāraṇas, besought them; thereupon those two best of gods desisted and came to peace."

sanskrit: jṛmbhitaṃ tad dhanur dṛṣṭvā śaivaṃ viṣṇuparākramaiḥ adhikaṃ menire viṣṇuṃ devāḥ sarṣigaṇās tadā
english: "Seeing that Śaiva bow made to yawn by the might of Viṣṇu, the gods and the hosts of sages then deemed Viṣṇu to be the greater."

sanskrit: dhanū rudras tu saṃkruddho videheṣu mahāyaśāḥ devarātasya rājarṣer dadau haste sasāyakam
english: "But Rudra, greatly angered, of immense glory, placed that bow together with its arrow into the hands of the royal sage Devarāta among the Videhas."

sanskrit: idaṃ ca viṣṇavaṃ rāma dhanuḥ parapuraṃjayam ṛcīke bhārgave prādād viṣṇuḥ sa nyāsam uttamam
english: "And this Vaiṣṇava bow, O Rāma, conqueror of enemy cities — Viṣṇu gave it as a most honoured trust to Ṛcīka of the Bhārgava line."

sanskrit: ṛcīkas tu mahātejāḥ putrasyāpratikarmaṇaḥ pitur mama dadau divyaṃ jamadagner mahātmanaḥ
english: "And Ṛcīka, of great splendour, gave that divine bow to the great-souled Jamadagni, my father, as a gift of inestimable service."

sanskrit: nyastaśastre pitari me tapobalasamanvite arjuno vidadhe mṛtyuṃ prākṛtāṃ buddhim āsthitaḥ
english: "While my father had laid aside his weapons and was endowed with the strength of asceticism, Arjuna, acting from a base mind, brought about his death."

sanskrit: vadham apratirūpaṃ tu pituḥ śrutvā sudāruṇam kṣatram utsādayaṃ roṣāj jātaṃ jātam anekaśaḥ
english: "Hearing of my father's wholly undeserved and terrible slaying, in wrath I exterminated the kṣatriyas time and again, generation after generation."

sanskrit: pṛthivīṃ cākhilāṃ prāpya kāśyapāya mahātmane yajñasyānte tadā rāma dakṣiṇāṃ puṇyakarmaṇe
english: "Having conquered the entire earth, O Rāma, at the conclusion of the sacrifice I then gave it as the sacrificial fee to the great-souled Kaśyapa, as the fruit of that pious act."

sanskrit: dattvā mahendranilayas tapobalasamanvitaḥ śrutavān dhanuṣo bhedaṃ tato 'haṃ drutam āgataḥ
english: "Having given the earth, I took up abode on mount Mahendra, endowed with the power of asceticism; then I heard of the breaking of the bow, and I came here swiftly."

sanskrit: tad idaṃ vaiṣṇavaṃ rāma pitṛpaitāmahaṃ mahat kṣatradharmaṃ puraskṛtya gṛhṇīṣva dhanuruttamam
english: "Therefore take this great Vaiṣṇava bow, O Rāma, which descended from father to grandfather — honouring the dharma of the kṣatriya, take this foremost of bows."

sanskrit: yojayasva dhanuḥ śreṣṭhe śaraṃ parapuraṃjayam yadi śaknoṣi kākutstha dvandvaṃ dāsyāmi te tataḥ
english: "Fit to this foremost bow the arrow that conquers enemy cities; if you are able, O Kākutstha, I shall then give you single combat."

sanskrit: śrutvā taj jāmadagnyasya vākyaṃ dāśarathis tadā gauravād yantritakathaḥ pitū rāmam athābravīt
english: Hearing those words of the son of Jamadagni, Daśaratha's son Rāma, his speech restrained out of deference to his father, then spoke.

sanskrit: śrutavān asmi yat karma kṛtavān asi bhārgava anurundhyāmahe brahman pitur ānṛṇyam āsthitaḥ
english: "I have heard of the deeds you have performed, O Bhārgava; I acknowledge them, O brahman — I stand here honouring my debt to my father."

sanskrit: vīryahīnam ivāśaktaṃ kṣatradharmeṇa bhārgava avajānāmi me tejaḥ paśya me 'dya parākramam
english: "You treat me as though I were devoid of valour and incapable, O Bhārgava, by the code of the kṣatriya — witness my splendour today; behold my prowess!"

sanskrit: ity uktvā rāghavaḥ kruddho bhārgavasya varāyudham śaraṃ ca pratisaṃgṛhya hastāl laghuparākramaḥ
english: Having spoken thus, the swift and mighty Rāghava in anger took from the hand of the Bhārgava both his supreme weapon and the arrow,

sanskrit: āropya sa dhanū rāmaḥ śaraṃ sajyaṃ cakāra ha jāmadagnyaṃ tato rāmaṃ rāmaḥ kruddho 'bravīd vacaḥ
english: and Rāma strung the bow and fitted the arrow to the string; then Rāma, enraged, spoke these words to Jāmadagnya Rāma.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇo 'sīti pūjyo me viśvāmitrakṛtena ca tasmāc chakto na te rāma moktuṃ prāṇaharaṃ śaram
english: "Because you are a brāhmaṇa you are venerable to me, and because of what Viśvāmitra has done for me — therefore, O Rāma, I am unable to release this life-taking arrow at you."

sanskrit: imāṃ vā tvadgatiṃ rāma tapobalasamārjitān lokān apratimān vāpi haniṣyāmi yad icchasi
english: "I shall destroy either this your freedom of movement, O Rāma, or those incomparable worlds accumulated by the power of your asceticism — whichever you wish."

sanskrit: na hy ayaṃ vaiṣṇavo divyaḥ śaraḥ parapuraṃjayaḥ moghaḥ patati vīryeṇa baladarpavināśanaḥ
english: "For this divine Vaiṣṇava arrow, conqueror of enemy cities, does not fall in vain by virtue of its might — it is the destroyer of the arrogance of strength."

sanskrit: varāyudhadharaṃ rāma draṣṭuṃ sarṣigaṇāḥ surāḥ pitāmahaṃ puraskṛtya sametās tatra saṃghaśaḥ
english: To behold Rāma bearing the supreme weapon, the hosts of sages and the gods, with Brahmā the Grandfather at their head, assembled there in multitudes.

sanskrit: gandharvāpsarasaś caiva siddhacāraṇakiṃnarāḥ yakṣarākṣasanāgāś ca tad draṣṭuṃ mahad adbhutam
english: Gandharvas, Apsarases, Siddhas, Cāraṇas, Kiṃnaras, Yakṣas, Rākṣasas, and Nāgas — all came to witness that great wonder.

sanskrit: jaḍīkṛte tadā loke rāme varadhanurdhare nirvīryo jāmadagnyo 'sau ramo rāmam udaikṣata
english: When the world had become stupefied, as Rāma held the bow of boons, that Jāmadagnya Rāma, now drained of valour, looked upon Rāma.

sanskrit: tejobhir hatavīryatvāj jāmadagnyo jaḍīkṛtaḥ rāmaṃ kamala patrākṣaṃ mandaṃ mandam uvāca ha
english: Stupefied, his power of valour struck down by Rāma's splendour, the son of Jamadagni slowly and softly spoke to Rāma of lotus-petal eyes.

sanskrit: kāśyapāya mayā dattā yadā pūrvaṃ vasuṃdharā viṣaye me na vastavyam iti māṃ kāśyapo 'bravīt
english: "When I previously gave the earth to Kaśyapa, Kaśyapa told me: 'You must not dwell within my domain.'"

sanskrit: so 'haṃ guruvacaḥ kurvan pṛthivyāṃ na vase niśām iti pratijñā kākutstha kṛtā vai kāśyapasya ha
english: "Honouring the word of my guru, this is the vow I made to Kaśyapa, O Kākutstha: 'I shall not spend even a single night upon the earth.'"

sanskrit: tad imāṃ tvaṃ gatiṃ vīra hantuṃ nārhasi rāghava manojavaṃ gamiṣyāmi mahendraṃ parvatottamam
english: "Therefore, O hero Rāghava, you should not destroy this my freedom of movement; swift as thought I shall depart to Mahendra, the greatest of mountains."

sanskrit: lokās tv apratimā rāma nirjitās tapasā mayā jahi tāñ śaramukhyena mā bhūt kālasya paryayaḥ
english: "But those incomparable worlds I have conquered through asceticism, O Rāma — destroy those with the foremost arrow; let there be no delay of time."

sanskrit: akṣayyaṃ madhuhantāraṃ jānāmi tvāṃ sureśvaram dhanuṣo 'sya parāmarśāt svasti te 'stu paraṃtapa
english: "I know you to be the eternal slayer of Madhu, the lord of the gods — by your very touch of this bow it is proven; may good befall you, O scorcher of foes."

sanskrit: ete suragaṇāḥ sarve nirīkṣante samāgatāḥ tvām apratimakarmāṇam apratidvandvam āhave
english: "All these hosts of gods have assembled and behold you, whose deeds are without equal and who has no rival in battle."

sanskrit: na ceyaṃ mama kākutstha vrīḍā bhavitum arhati tvayā trailokyanāthena yad ahaṃ vimukhīkṛtaḥ
english: "Nor should this be a source of shame for me, O Kākutstha, that I have been turned back by you — you who are the lord of the three worlds."

sanskrit: śaram apratimaṃ rāma moktum arhasi suvrata śaramokṣe gamiṣyāmi mahendraṃ parvatottamam
english: "You should release this peerless arrow, O Rāma of noble vow; once the arrow is released I shall depart to mount Mahendra, the greatest of mountains."

sanskrit: tathā bruvati rāme tu jāmadagnye pratāpavān rāmo dāśarathiḥ śrīmāṃś cikṣepa śaram uttamam
english: While Jāmadagnya Rāma was speaking thus, the glorious and mighty Rāma, son of Daśaratha, released that supreme arrow.

sanskrit: tato vitimirāḥ sarvā diśā copadiśas tathā surāḥ sarṣigaṇā rāmaṃ praśaśaṃsur udāyudham
english: Then all the directions and intermediate quarters became free of darkness; the gods and hosts of sages praised Rāma as he held his weapon aloft.

sanskrit: rāmaṃ dāśarathiṃ rāmo jāmadagnyaḥ praśasya ca tataḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya jagāmātmagatiṃ prabhuḥ
english: And Rāma the son of Jamadagni, having praised Rāma the son of Daśaratha, then circumambulated him clockwise and departed, that lord, to his own abode.
